summary.oneLiner: GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Limited is the Indian subsidiary of GSK plc, a science-led global healthcare company, holding market-leading positions in Private Vaccines, Anti-Infectives and Dermatology while scaling a specialty portfolio in Oncology and Respiratory care.
summary.business: GSK operates across three business verticals in India — General Medicines, Vaccines and Specialty Medicines — spanning preventive healthcare (vaccines), primary care and advanced curative/specialty therapies. The General Medicines portfolio (Anti-Infectives, Pain Management, Hormones, Dermatology) anchors the business and contributes more than 80% of revenue, while the Company is building out Adult Vaccines, Respiratory Care and, since 2025, Oncology as newer growth engines.

currentContext.strengths: Strong portfolio of flagship, HCP-endorsed brands (Augmentin, Calpol, Ceftum, Betnovate, Neosporin, T-bact, Tenovate, Boostrix, Infanrix Hexa, Varilrix, Havrix) underpinning market leadership in Private Vaccines, Anti-Infectives and Dermatology|Global scale and expertise as a subsidiary of GSK plc, benefiting from parent-group resources and R&D|Robust and integrated omnichannel marketing ecosystem combining in-person HCP engagement with digital platforms (webinars, podcasts, virtual learning)|Digital-led innovation ecosystem integrating AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics (Minerva, GiGi, Rep Copilot) into commercial operations
currentContext.strategies: Sustaining General Medicines as the revenue backbone (>80% of revenue) through continued high-quality scientific engagement, HCP endorsement and digital enablement|Scaling Specialty Medicines (Oncology and Respiratory) as the next frontier for precision-led growth, supported by a Patient Support Programme and CARE accounts to improve access, adherence and outcomes|Strengthening the adult vaccination ecosystem, recalibrating strategy to focus on cardiovascular-and-metabolic-disease (CVMD) risk cohorts for shingles prevention, and closing gaps in maternal and second-year childhood immunisation|Building a robust and diversified supply chain via stronger contingency planning, alternate manufacturing options and improved end-to-end visibility, following FY2025-26 supply disruptions that had a material impact on performance|Accelerating the innovation pipeline across Oncology, Vaccines and liver disease management through new launches and clinical trial participation|Driving digital-first, AI-enabled commercial operations (Minerva, GiGi, Rep Copilot) to improve field effectiveness and HCP engagement|Building a performance-led culture through structured succession planning, high-potential talent identification and technology-enabled leadership development|Contributing to India's Viksit Bharat @2047 mission by investing in next-generation therapies, new access models and digital enablement|Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (approved 27th October 2016) and recommends dividends annually to Members, subject to AGM approval; a Rs. 57 per equity share final dividend was recommended for FY2025-26, to be voted on at the 101st AGM on 30th June 2026. As part of its oversight function, the Board reviews the strategy, annual business plan and capital expenditure budgets.
currentContext.expansion: FY2025-26 marked GSK's foray into Oncology in India with the launch of Jemperli (dostarlimab) and Zejula (niraparib), including launch engagements across 50+ centres, the introduction of the Phoenix Patient Support Programme, and access expansion through CARE ecosystems (CGHS, ECHS, ESIC). On Vaccines, the Company scaled its digital ordering platform VaxiKart (12,000+ HCPs onboarded, now ~45% of paediatric vaccine revenues) and its 7-Star Awareness Campaign across 3,000+ paediatric clinics, and is exploring new adult-vaccination access channels via hospital partnerships, armed forces and railways. At the Nashik manufacturing site, the Company installed a 300 kW solar power system, a 66 KLD sewerage treatment plant for domestic wastewater treatment, and a 900 TR advanced cooling tower, and upgraded the electrical/control panel on the Alexander Werk Roll Compactor used in Albendazole manufacturing and added electronic data integration for in-process quality-check instruments at Eltroxin manufacturing.

risks.risk: Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty in major markets
risks.note: Governments, particularly in the US and EU, are prioritising domestic drug manufacturing and supply-chain localisation amid tariff uncertainty and trade tensions, creating policy risk for the globally integrated biopharma supply chains GSK's India operations are part of.
Despite governments viewing biopharma as a key growth engine, growing pressure on drug pricing continues across major markets, a structural constraint on industry margins.

As a large manufacturer of antibiotics, the Company faces regulatory and reputational risk tied to AMR; its global strategy commits to certifying all internal antibiotic-manufacturing sites by end of 2026, with the Nashik site newly awarded the BSI Kitemark for seven antimicrobial products, subject to annual surveillance audits to retain certification.

The Company is preparing for operationalisation of India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, 2025, requiring strengthened data-privacy/security governance, alongside continued compliance with the Uniform Code of Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP) 2024.
A Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) process is applied during vendor onboarding, indicating reliance on and exposure to external vendors and supply partners.

risks.risk: Dependence on parent-level (GSK plc) risk and control frameworks
risks.note: The Company's Internal Control Framework, Independent Business Monitoring and Management Monitoring exercises are approved/designed by the Global GSK Leadership Team and the Global Risk Oversight and Compliance Council (ROCC), reflecting structural dependence on group-level governance for local risk oversight.

one-line thesis: GSK India delivered its first INR1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, driven by supply normalization in GenMeds and strong oncology vaccine launches, with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.9% — the key change is the transition from volume-driven generics to high-margin specialty assets like Zejula/Jemperli and Shingrix, which now define future growth and margin sustainability.
financial scorecard: revenue: +8.1% YoY (INR1,000cr milestone); EBITDA/margin: +26.7% YoY to 35.9% (520bps expansion, one-off labour cost impact of INR11.8cr excluded); PAT: +290bps to 27.3% margin; order book: not disclosed; net debt: INR2,426cr cash position (net debt negative)
guidance: revenue growth: 12-13% CAGR over 5 years to reach INR8,000cr; margin: sustain 35%+ range; order inflow: not disclosed; capex/commissioning: no new capex announced, focus on digital and field force optimization
segment / subsidiary detail: GenMeds: +9% market growth, brands Augmentin/Ceftum/T-Bact grew double digits; Vaccines: +11% YoY, led by Boostrix/Varilrix/Havrix; Shingrix: ~INR75cr annual run rate (CY25), 80% growth YoY, now tied to CVMD strategy; Specialty: Zejula/Jemperli launched in Q3, first full quarter with 250+ patients on therapy; Jemperli gained first-line endometrial cancer approval in Dec 2025, expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; pipeline includes Belantamab (multiple myeloma), Bepirovirsen (chronic Hep B functional cure), RSV vaccine, Efimosfermin (liver disease)
growth verticals / optionality: Oncology: Belantamab (Blenrep) launch expected in FY27; liver disease: Bepirovirsen (first functional cure for Hep B) and Efimosfermin in pipeline; RSV vaccine nearing approval; 12-15 indications for next-gen ADC B3H7 over 5 years; oncology indications expanding to rectal cancer (2026 readout)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin at 35.9% (highest in 2 years), driven by gross margin improvement and disciplined cost control; no material impact from MIP on Amoxiclav; raw material prices stable for 2 years; injectables have lower margins than base GenMeds due to higher launch costs, but base business size dilutes impact
capex / expansion: no new capex announced; focus on digital infrastructure and field force optimization; existing Nashik plant supports India-for-India model; no plans for new manufacturing facilities
capital allocation: prioritizing investment in specialty commercial teams (oncology, hematology); funding patient assistance programs; maintaining strong cash position (INR2,426cr); no dividend or buyback guidance given
risks & watch-items: NLEM price cuts remain structural risk for GenMeds (though current portfolio is NLEM-resilient); supply chain dependency on CMOs (past fire incident caused INR25-30cr revenue loss); oncology adoption speed dependent on HCP education and reimbursement; currency and API price volatility
management quality / tone: highly confident, transformational, and disciplined; management emphasizes sustainability over margin expansion, highlights portfolio shift from volume to value, and frames oncology/vaccines as future growth engines; tone is strategic, data-driven, and investor-aligned
non-obvious takeaways: Shingrix’s CVMD linkage is a unique commercial differentiator — not just a vaccine but a preventive cardiology tool; oncology field force is tiny (25 KAS) but highly targeted (1,000 oncologists), enabling high ROI despite low headcount; digital touchpoints (4M/quarter) now complement and extend field force, reducing need for large-scale MR expansion

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global medicine market expected to grow at 5-8% CAGR to reach about USD 2.4 Trillion by 2029, with specialty medicines rising to ~46% of global spending by 2029 from 27% in 2014
- Rising chronic illness (cancer, chronic respiratory disease, neurological illness) projected to account for the top ten global disease burdens by 2032, keeping oncology a top biopharma innovation priority alongside new technologies such as antibody drug conjugates
- Growing risk from infectious disease, vaccine-preventable outbreaks and antimicrobial resistance is accelerating the industry-wide shift toward preventive healthcare
- Advances in AI and automation are expected to improve R&D and manufacturing efficiency across biopharma in the near-to-medium term
- India's economy remained resilient in FY2025-26 on tax reforms, GST rationalisation, infrastructure spending and new Free Trade Agreements with the UK and EU, with IMF projecting India GDP growth of 6.5% in 2026 and 2027
- Indian pharmaceutical industry evolving from manufacturing hub to global innovation hub, with the domestic market projected to grow from ~USD 60 Billion to ~USD 130 Billion by 2030
- Structural demand tailwinds: India's population aged 50+ projected to rise from 193 million (2011) to 404 million by 2036, alongside rising life expectancy and disease burden
- Expanding healthcare access and affordability via government schemes (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covering 120 million families) and digital health infrastructure investment (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, National Biopharma Mission)
- Union Budget 2026-27 repositions biopharma/biologics as a core national pillar, including a Rs. 100 Billion Biopharma SHAKTI outlay, 1,000+ accredited clinical trial sites, customs duty exemption on 17 cancer drugs, and Rs. 47,700 million for the PM-ABHIM health infrastructure mission
- 26 ongoing and planned global and local clinical trials being conducted in India, including trials for Bepirovirsen, an investigational antisense oligonucleotide targeting a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B
- Jemperli progressing through approval for expanded indications across other solid tumours, following first-line approval for primary advanced and recurrent endometrial cancer
- Pipeline acceleration underway in Oncology, Vaccines and liver disease management, including the upcoming Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin) launch in haemato-oncology and the entry of Arexvy (RSV vaccine for older/high-risk adults)

On Vaccines, the Company scaled its digital ordering platform VaxiKart (12,000+ HCPs onboarded, now ~45% of paediatric vaccine revenues) and its 7-Star Awareness Campaign across 3,000+ paediatric clinics, and is exploring new adult-vaccination access channels via hospital partnerships, armed forces and railways. other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership] Bhushan Akshikar has been MD of GSK India since Q3 2022 (15+ years at GSK across India, Middle East, Russia CIS and Africa; prior 15 years at Johnson & Johnson); Ronojit Biswas has been CFO since April 2026, previously Senior Finance Director – Global Product Strategy for General Medicines and CFO for GSK's Brazil and Vietnam businesses.
- [Market context] The deck reports IPM grew 13.5% in Q1 FY27 and separately shows IPM growth of 13.6% for Apr-May'26 attributed largely to price (Volume 8.7%, NI 1.9%, Price 3.0% are the components shown); chronic (40% of industry, 15% growth) grew better than acute (60%, 11%) and MNCs (16% share, 17% growth) grew ahead of Indian players (84% share, 13%).
- [Slide without content] The deck carries an 'Upcoming Launches' slide whose contents did not survive text extraction, so the pipeline/launch detail is not available here.
